title: Labyrinth
build: Two-sided English disk edition; stored credit at $743D-$747D includes V 1.0 V; supplied G64 preservation images

records.c: M3 map/header resource, 510 unpacked bytes. The captured first64-cell strip includes arrival column35 cell0 (wall) and neighboring column36 cell7, translated as closed-door type2. Live OPEN DOOR at X2348/depth24 changed column36 to cell6, translated as open-door type3. Other map fields remain partial.

Captured arrival column12 has cell1, translated through $073F as type11. The door-shaped spiral panel pictured here is rejected by ASK DOOR's type2/3 prerequisite; OPEN DOOR separately returns Nothing happens. Up for300 frames reaches depth24 without an exit from this position. Other actions and return routes remain unverified.

Sixteen replacement cell nibbles indexed by the current cell's low nibble in OPEN DOOR's type-two branch. Captured index7 contains6, changing the neighboring closed door to open-door type3 through $073E.

Sixteen replacements indexed by the original cell low nibble when CLOSE DOOR sees translated type3. In the captured map, open cell4 becomes closed5 and open6 becomes closed7. Mutation $58C8 masks the replacement to its low nibble. Live column36 closing used6 to7.

Sixteen map-low-nibble translations. In the captured Brick Hallway, nibble0 translates to wall type0, nibble7 to closed-door type2, and nibble6 to open-door type3. OPEN DOOR branches on these translated types.
Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds. Column36 selects region11, whose threshold is36. The resolver scans fifteen entries then falls back to index15.

Sixteen source selectors. Region11 has selector1, choosing bits $60 of state $0500. The opened column36 exit does not call PRNG directly; the gameplay meaning and producer of that source byte remain open here.

Four interleaved banks, each sixteen scene requests followed by sixteen entry IDs, at stride32. For region11: scene request0 in every bank, entry12 in banks0/1 and44 in banks2/3. These are entries within retained scene3, not room identifiers. Other routes remain unverified.
Jump to $0998 to obtain the player's classified map cell: A is its low nibble, X its translated type, Y the column. OPEN DOOR uses this result through the resident API.
Jump to $09A5, which calls $58C8 with A replacement cell and Y column. Additional scene-eleven/twenty-three handling in that wrapper is outside this Brick Hallway check.
Jump to $09E9. Some door commands call this as a prerequisite; OPEN DOOR uses its separate type check at $9053.
Call classifier $4171, load its column $AF into Y, read $0600,Y and mask to its low nibble in A; return translated type $B0 in X. This query contains no approach-depth threshold.

Call $58C8. For current scene3, skip the scene-eleven/twenty-three special cases and enter $09D0, requesting zero through $0530. This is consumed as the resident redraw/reload path; live OPEN DOOR retained current scene3 and its player position while updating the door picture. Other scenes' special cases remain outside this check.
Write zero to pending scene request $0530 and return. This is the request produced after the Brick Hallway door-cell mutation, not a claim that the player travels to another room.
Set response mode5, then $09DF stores Y/X as the low/high pointer at $10/$11 and tail-calls message queue $674C. The failed door prerequisite enters here with pointer $0D49.

In negative map mode $0343, query the player cell through $0998 and accept translated type3 or2 by returning at $0A02. Otherwise select message $0D49, pull the helper caller's return address off the stack and tail-call $09DD, bypassing the rest of that command handler. At the natural column12 arrival, cell1 translates to type11 and fails this check. This is a command prerequisite, not proof that every other action or route is impossible.
Headered message whose original-parser expansion is There's no door here. The failed $09E9 prerequisite uses this message. It includes a dictionary reference for door.

Negative $0343 mode scans inclusive column thresholds at $074E through indices0..14, falling back to15. Selector $076E chooses zero, state $0500, state $0501, or PRNG for values at least3. Mask with $60 to form a four-bank offset, combine the region index and write entry from $078E to $0532 and scene request from $077E to $0530. At opened column36, region11/selector1 uses $0500; all banks request0, with entry12 in banks0/1 and44 in banks2/3. Request0 with current scene3 is repositioning in that room, confirmed live to entry12.
Mutable region index cached by $4115 while choosing a banked route.

Set Y zero and enter $4173. In the captured negative $0343 mode, derive column (world X shifted right six) masked by $5E, retain the map cell at $B7, translate its low nibble through $073E into $B0 and obtain the depth bound/flag. Other map modes remain partial.
Sixteen bounds indexed by classified type, with negative types using zero. Captured ordinary wall type zero and closed-door type two have limit24; open-door type three has limit40.

Sixteen flags paired with $41F0. Captured type zero/two have negative flags, while open-door type three has zero, allowing the captured negative-$0385 depth-bound path to request an exit. Complete traversal through the opened door remains unverified.

For request $0530 zero and positive current scene $0531=3, jump to $53CE to place objects and rebuild the view while retaining that scene. Nonzero requests take $5103; negative/zero current scenes take $50F9, whose effects are outside this check. Live door traversal reached request0/entry12 and retained current scene3.

Call placement $543A, activate player slot $0248 and clear drawing-disable state $0310 before continuing the resident redraw/camera path at $53DB. The observed request0/entry12 positions the player at X800/depth6 in scene3; remaining camera/redraw logic is not described here.

For slots2..0, skip $FF entries at $5080. In nonnegative mode, compute X=64*entry+32 and depth6 for player slot0 or24 for other slots; initialize origins, fractional fields and active flags. Clear request entry $0532 after all slots. Negative-mode branches remain outside the corridor widget. Live door traversal selected entry12 and placed the player at X800/depth6.

Mask A to low nibble, cache value/column at $5928/$5929 and write $0600,Y. Scenes below2 or equal4 return. Otherwise search 84 entries at $0400 for matching scene and column $0455; update value $04AA on a match. If none matches, use a zero scene slot, or repeatedly sample PRNG bits below84 until finding a record from another scene; store current scene, column and replacement value. This describes the mutation record write, not a full save/load proof.
Two mutable bytes: replacement map nibble and column cached by $58C8 for the scene/column/value record update.
Action/object pair [30,45] for ASK DOOR; parallel pointer $8BCC selects $8DD1.
CLOSE DOOR action/object pair [32,45]. Parallel pointer $8BEE selects $8E9E. Ordinary input at the opened column36 door reached this handler twice in the checked CLOSE,CLOSE,OPEN,OPEN sequence.
Action/object pairs [37,45] then [37,0]. The first matches OPEN DOOR and selects handler $9053 via $8C54; the second is the following OPEN wildcard response. The dispatcher scans in stored order.
Pointer to ASK DOOR handler $8DD1, paired with $8B0C.
Pointer to CLOSE DOOR handler $8E9E, paired with $8B2E.
Handler $9053 for OPEN DOOR, followed by fallback message selector $14BB for OPEN with another object. The pairs live at $8B94.

Call prerequisite $082A. Accepted door types2/3 return and select response $94BB, Nothing happens. A failed prerequisite bypasses this continuation and queues $0D49, There's no door here. Ordinary ASK DOOR at column12/type11 displayed that rejection, with one handler dispatch and one prerequisite hit.

Nonnegative $0343 selects fallback $94BB through $8ECC. In negative mode, query $0818. Translated type3 selects replacement $072E+cellNibble, mutates through $081B, requests sound2 and decrements opened-door counter $0569. Type2 instead selects $92E0, It's already closed.; other types select $94BB, Nothing happens. Response path $8ECC jumps to $91C7. Ordinary column36 close changed cell6 to7/count4 to3; repeat close retained7/3. Reopening restored6/4; repeating OPEN retained6/4. This handler contains no depth comparison; ordinary reachability is checked only at the stated door approach.

Nonnegative map mode $0343 selects fallback message pointer $94BB. Otherwise query the player cell through $0818. Type2 indexes replacement table $071E by the cell nibble, calls mutation API $081B, requests sound1 through $081E and increments $0569. Type3 selects pointer $92CA; other types select $94BB. Both response branches use $9081. This handler has no depth comparison; the tested ordinary door approach reached X2348/depth24.
Tail-jump to $91C7, which selects response mode5 and calls message API $0827 with the pointer in X/Y. Text expansion is outside this partial handler annotation.

Load mode5 in A and tail-call response API $0827 with the low/high pointer in Y/X. CLOSE DOOR reaches this through $8ECC for its already-closed and fallback messages; other callers remain outside this check.
Headered message whose original-parser expansion is It's already closed. Live second CLOSE DOOR at column36 displayed this and retained counter3/cell7, with a handler hit but no new map mutation.
